question: Mikrovlnná rúra vznikla vlastne náhodou: americkému inžinierovi, ktorý pracoval s radarom, sa zrazu niečo roztopilo vo vrecku. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: Accounts say he was standing near an active magnetron at Raytheon when a bar in his pocket melted.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume such a common appliance was carefully designed as a cooker. In fact it began as a radar accident with a melted snack, and players can guess the snack from everyday logic: what melts in a pocket?
extra.verification_notes: Spencer's melted candy bar (commonly chocolate; some retellings say a peanut cluster bar) is the standard origin story; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percy_Spencer

explanation: Percy Spencer si všimol, že mu pri radarovom magnetróne zmäkla čokoládová tyčinka. Hneď nato tam skúsil dať kukuricu a urobil prvé pukance z mikrovlnky.

question: Rýchlovarná kanvica sa sama vypne presne vtedy, keď voda zovrie, hoci teplotu vody vôbec nemeria. Čo ju v skutočnosti vypne?
source_excerpt: steam from the boiling water travels down a tube and actuates the bimetallic disc that disconnects the power supply

extra.why_interesting: Everyone uses a kettle daily and assumes it has a thermometer in the water. The real trigger is the steam, and a player can reason the way there: what appears exactly when water boils?
extra.verification_notes: Kettle auto-off is triggered by steam reaching a bimetallic switch, per https://www.ingenia.org.uk/articles/how-do-kettles-know-when-to-switch-off; no newer developments found that contradict this.

explanation: Para z vriacej vody prúdi úzkym kanálikom k bimetalovému plátku pri rúčke. Ten sa teplom prehne a cvakne vypínačom. Preto kanvica s otvoreným vekom niekedy vrie ďalej.
